newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London mixed in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London mixed in active trade.

text.p: Japanese stocks in London had mixed fortunes in active trade on Friday, with interest shifting from dollar-sensitive exporter issues to the construction sector, traders said.

The Nikkei 50 index of leading shares traded in London edged some 5.76 points, or 0.40 percent, above Thursday's London close, after the Tokyo Nikkei 225 index ended some 17.17 points, or 0.09 percent lower.
Bank and construction stocks outperformed in Tokyo overnight, with both sectors sharply higher, but a cagey London open saw profit taking in banks, traders said.
"Construction stocks saw some follow-though buying after Tokyo," one trader said. "It looks as though construction buying will continue, but banks may slow down."

Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) fell sharply from Tokyo levels, and was sold heavily across the board on the back of a rumour that Nomura Bank International Plc will on Monday downgrade MHI from its current "buy" recommendation, dealers said.
MHI was some 32 yen below its Tokyo close at 855 yen by 1607 GMT.
Looking to Monday, traders said they expected to see continued interest in banks and construction, but think exporter issues will come off in the face of a weaker dollar/yen.
